title: Tim Curry Honored by Past and Present Frank-N-Furters With “I’m Going Home” Performance
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All August 27, 2026 12:20pm The 'Rocky Horror Show' Broadway cast pays tribute to Tim Curry. Rocky Horror Broadway/Instagram Luke Evans, Paul Soileau and Jake Shears paid tribute to late Rocky Horror Show star Tim Curry on Wednesday following news of his death at age 80. Following Wednesday‘s Broadway performance of The Rocky Horror Show , Paul Soileau — who is currently starring as Dr. Frank-N-Furter, the role Curry originated — honored the late actor after the curtain call. In videos shared online, Soileau told the audience, “The role of Frank-N-Furter is a marvelous beast. Frank-N-Furter inhabits spaces and sneaks in spaces and places and old theater houses and old theaters like this, movie theaters, teenagers’ bedrooms.“ Related Stories Lifestyle Pulitzer Prize Finalist 'Here There Are Blueberries' Set For Broadway Lifestyle 'Six' Will End Five-Year Broadway Run in January He added, “The way Frank-N-Furter survives is that he finds vessels and he goes into them and he takes them over and he keeps moving and moving and moving all around. And many people in this room, on this stage, have been a vessel for Frank-N-Furter over the years. But if you trace it all back, 53 years ago, there’s one home and one vessel. One mothership that Frank-N-Furter could actually call home, and it’s Tim Curry.” Curry first took on the Frank-N-Furter role in the original 1973 London production of Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show , following a turn on Broadway in 1975 and in the 1975 film adaptation, The Rocky Horror Picture Show . “53 years ago, Richard O’Brien laid a piece of paper in front of Tim Curry with ingredients on it,” Soileau also said. “And he took all those ingredients and he created this beast that everyone found something within it and could see a piece of themselves inside of it.” Soileau later welcomed Luke Evans , who portrayed Frank-N-Furter in the current revival and played his final performance just three days prior, and Jake Shears, who will take over the role starting Sept. 11. Together, the past and present Frank-N-Furters performed the song “I’m Going Home,” from the musical. The performance was shared on the official social media accounts for the production. View this post on Instagram Rocky Horror creator Richard O’Brien also paid tribute to Curry in a message shared by his son online. “Tim Curry was a wonderful man by nature who was also a wonderful performer and understood the difference between such delightful achievements. He never sought attention and never put himself before the roles that he played. He was, in short, a good egg and class act,“ O’Brien said. “It was both a privilege and delight to have known him and worked with him. Rest in peace dear Tim.” On Wednesday, a tribute to Curry was also set up at Rocky Horror ‘s Studio 54 Broadway theater. Tribute to Tim Curry in lobby of Broadway Theater THR Staff THR

title: Andrea Eastman, Casting Director on ‘The Godfather’ and Former ICM Agent, Dies at 86
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 12:15pm Andrea Eastman Patrick McMullan/Getty Images Andrea Eastman, who as the head of casting at Paramount Pictures brought Ali MacGraw to Goodbye, Columbus and James Caan to The Godfather before serving as a manager and longtime ICM agent, has died. She was 86. Eastman died Wednesday in her sleep at her home in Santa Barbara, a family spokesperson told The Hollywood Reporter . A real straight-shooter, Eastman discovered Jaclyn Smith, got Steven Spielberg and Roy Scheider together for Jaws (1975), managed Sylvester Stallone in his Rocky heyday and talked Rob Reiner into hiring her client — and his best friend — Billy Crystal for When Harry Met Sally … (1989). Related Stories Movies Samuel Monroe Jr., 'Menace II Society' Star, Dies at 52 Movies Peter Cullen, Voice of Optimus Prime in 'Transformers,' Dies at 85 With a long stint at ICM in Los Angeles and New York, she also repped and/or managed Barbra Streisand, Burt Reynolds , Peter Boyle, Chevy Chase, Henry Winkler, Jamie Lee Curtis, Christopher Reeve, Katharine Ross, Christopher Plummer , James Brolin, Dustin Hoffman, Dyan Cannon, Gabriel Byrne, Brenda Vaccaro, Richard Gere, Kim Basinger, Kathleen Turner, Stockard Channing, Tony Danza, Wes Craven, Katherine Heigl, Katie Couric, Elle MacPherson, Marshall Brickman and Charlie Rose, among many others over the years. Eastman fought to cast MacGraw, then a 30-year-old photographer’s assistant and model new to acting, for the role of the younger Jewish-American princess Brenda Patimkin opposite Richard Benjamin as her romantic interest Neil Klugman in Goodbye, Columbus (1969), directed by Larry Peerce. Natalie Wood had already turned down the part, and the studio had looked at hundreds of other actresses before MacGraw came aboard. (The year the movie hit theaters, MacGraw wed Paramount Studios chief Robert Evans .) Eastman initiated the casting for Francis Ford Coppola’s The Godfather (1972) and worked with Fred Roos to hire actors for the eventual Oscar winner for best picture. “You make endless lists when you are a casting director,” she said in 2023. “When you do a movie, you try to think out of the box. For The Godfather , it was endless casting. We worked seven days a week. I was dreaming of Italians all night every night.” Eastman thought Italian producer Carlo Ponti would make a great Vito Corleone before Godfather author Mario Puzo came up with the idea to cast Marlon Brando . Caan had excelled in his screen test for the film and was slated to play Michael Corleone opposite the hulking Carmine Caridi as Sonny Corleone (Coppola had offered him the role in a bar). But when Al Pacino was hired to play Michael, Caan was out of the movie. Caridi “was a big guy but not menacing. He was like a big Saint Bernard,” Eastman said. “Luckily, he’d never formally signed a deal, and Coppola trusted me. He was leaving for Sicily [to scout locations], so he told me, ‘Just cast my fucking movie!’” After getting Charlie Bluhdorn, head of Paramount parent Gulf + Western, and Evans to sign off on Caan as Sonny and Pacino as Michael, Eastman hurriedly got Caan to sign a contract before someone changed their mind. “We all worked as a team, but I am responsible for Jimmy Caan getting the part of Sonny,” she said. This era was the happiest time in her career, she often noted, but she would quit the studio in early 1973. Born on June 15, 1940, Eastman grew up in Westport, Connecticut, where she attended Staples High School. She graduated from Ohio State University and married producer and backgammon expert Bruce Becker; after they divorced, she moved to California. In summer 1968, she was working as an assistant for $150 a week for Paramount head of casting Joyce Selznick when the niece of Gone With the Wind producer David O. Selznick was fired. Eastman, then 28, took her place and made $300 a week. She first spotted Smith when both were in the audience at the stage musical Hallelujah, Baby! “She was gorgeous,” Eastman said in an interview last year. “I walked up to her and gave her my card. She looked at me like, ‘Who is this person? She’s my age.’ And then I brought her in and she met Charlie Bluhdorn and Bob Evans and we put her under contract.” (Smith would play as a wedding guest in Goodbye, Columbus. ) Eastman’s tenure at Paramount also saw the release of such notable films as True Grit (1969), Downhill Racer (1969), the box office sensation (and MacGraw-starring) Love Story (1970), Catch 22 (1970), T.R. Baskin (1971) and Play It Again, Sam (1972). She said she quit Paramount when Frank Yablans , who had recently replaced Stanley R. Jaffe as studio chief, threatened to fire her if she attended the 1973 Academy Awards, where The Godfather was nominated for 11 Oscars. She took a job at double her previous salary as an agent at International Famous Agency; her clients back then included Ross, Boyle, Curtis, Benjamin and Paula Prentiss. She left to become Stallone’s manager, and that led to her agreeing in 1977 to form a joint personal management company with Jeff Wald , Ron DiBlasio and Herb Nanas. But soon after introducing Stallone to Wald, she was told by DiBlasio that “we don’t want to go forward with you, Jeff’s going to have his own company,” she recalled in 2023. She said she was offered $25,000 but turned that down, and she would file a $1 million suit against Wald and DiBlasio for damages. She formed her own company, Andrea Eastman Management, before joining ICM in 1983. She said Spielberg offered Scheider the role of police chief Martin Brody in Jaws at one of her dinner parties and that Reiner gave Crystal his script to When Harry Met Sally at one of her weddings. Later, she convinced Streisand to appear in an unglamorous role in Meet the Frockers (2004). Eastman moved to Bozeman, Montana, full-time in 2005 and retired from ICM in 2010. Her husbands also included attorney Richard Wilsker and producer Paul N. Lazarus III ( Westworld , Capricorn One ). In the 2022 Paramount+ miniseries The Offer , Eastman was portrayed by Stephanie Koenig. She said she did not appreciate that she and Godfather producer Al Ruddy were depicted as having a one-night stand when it fact they had love affair that lasted more than a year. She established a sanctuary in Montana near Big Sky Resort dedicated to rescuing, rehabilitating and sheltering maltreated, abandoned and abused horses and dogs, and her impact as an animal advocate was chronicled in Jill Rappaport’s 2004 book, People We Know, Horses They Love . In the late 1990s, she enlisted Robert Redford ’s help in getting the nation’s first state initiative to ban the slaughter of horses for human consumption passed. She spent three months in 2020 at the Beverly Hills Hotel recovering from open-heart surgery. Her late golden retriever had the run of the place, which was operating at a limited capacity during COVID, and a kids picture book written from the pooch’s perspective, Trooper at the Beverly Hills Hotel , was published in 2022. After some tough early years in Hollywood, Eastman proved to be as tough as they come. “One of the things [you learn] being an agent is you don’t give up,” she said in 2014. “You never take no for an answer.” THR

title: ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks
full_text: Aug 27, 2026 12:14pm PT ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks 29 minutes ago What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’ 1 hour ago New York Comic Con Unveils 2026 Professional Schedule Lineup, Including ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ Author-NBCUniversal TV Panel (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago See All Rockstar Games Netflix dropped 27 minutes of new “Grand Theft Auto 6” content Thursday at 3 p.m. ET in a collaboration with Rockstar Games ahead of the highly anticipated title’s November release. The event, which was first announced earlier this month, comes as Rockstar continues to suffer ongoing “ GTA 6 ” gameplay leaks. The content was captured entirely from in-game footage on PlayStation 5 (the game will be released for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S on Nov. 19), per Netflix and Take-Two Interactive-owned publisher Rockstar. It marks the lengthiest look fans have gotten at “GTA 6” thus far, following two trailers released over the past three years. Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 The official description for “GTA 6” reads: “Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida – forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.” Popular on Variety Rockstar has stated Netflix will be the exclusive home of the “Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look” special for six hours before the content is released on YouTube and across other platforms. It seems that exclusivity has had an impact as user error reports for Netflix spiked just prior to the Netflix “GTA 6” reveal, hitting 3,129 at 2:49 p.m. ET, according to service-monitoring website Downdetector.com. Netflix says the “GTA 6” “extended look” event represents “the next evolution of storytelling and content” on the streaming platform: “This trailblazing partnership with Rockstar Games elevates games to the center of modern culture — bringing an in-depth look at one of the most anticipated releases in the history of entertainment to Netflix subscribers first.” Rockstar Games — which last week filed subpoenas related to the leaks — issued its first statement about the situation on Wednesday: “Dear all, We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week. It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has — from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know. We are very excited for everyone to see the extended look tomorrow. It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19. We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week — your words meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games. We look forward to sharing more with you soon. Sincerely, Rockstar Games” Later that day, Rockstar posted two messages on X noting its preferences regarding how fans go about creating content based on the Netflix event amid the outside leaks, writing: “Once Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look debuts on Netflix, creators can share their reaction content across social and video platforms.” In a followup, Rockstar added: “Quick clarification: you are free to livestream An Extended Look from 3 p.m. ET on August 27 providing you adhere to platform-specific guidance and you do not simply restream or repost the unedited video in full without context or commentary.” More to come… Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Raye Make Mercury Prize Shortlist Loading comments... title: ‘Furious’ Renewed for Second Season at Hulu
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 12:00pm Emmy Rossum in Hulu's 'Furious' Sarah Shatz/Disney Logo text Hulu is still feeling Furious . The Disney-owned streamer has renewed Furious , a serial killer thriller starring Emmy Rossum , for a second season. The pickup comes a few days ahead of the first season finale, which debuts Aug. 31. Loosely based on the 1987 movie Black Widow and created by Elizabeth Meriwether , Furious stars Rossum as Alice Black, an FBI agent who is tracking a serial killer (played by Lola Petticrew). “Both walk their own paths toward justice,” the show’s logline reads, “and as their lives start to intertwine, the line between right and wrong begins to blur.” Related Stories TV 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' Season 5 Trailer Teases Leadup to Taylor Frankie Paul's 'Bachelorette' Season Being Pulled TV Mindy Kaling and 'Not Suitable for Work' Cast React to Cancellation: "I Loved Making This Show" The second season is likely to follow Rossum’s Alice on a new case, though it’s still very early in the development process. Furious has received strong reviews; The Hollywood Reporter critic Daniel Fienberg wrote that “especially in its home stretch, [the series] becomes a complex, well-acted and even funny thriller about the ongoing toll of trauma, the psychic cost of revenge and the danger of a life driven by anger.” Sources say the show is also likely to appear in Nielsen’s top 10 streaming charts for its premiere week; that data is due for release later Thursday. Season one of Furious also stars Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Scoot McNairy. Jake Lacy, Rob Delaney, Hope Davis, Rob Yang and Steve Way have recurring roles. “I love serial killer shows, but I’d never seen one with a female serial killer other than Killing Eve ,” Meriwether said on THR’ s podcast I’m Having an Episode earlier this month. “I wanted to dive into that character and [ Black Widow ] seemed like a good framework. This sounds insane, but the more I learned about female serial killers, the more I was drawn in — especially learning that most female serial killers have been victims of violence. That idea began forming in my head, just the cycle of violence and how misunderstood it is when it comes to women.” The series comes from 20th Television and Searchlight Television. Meriwether ( The Dropout, Dying for Sex, New Girl ) is the showrunner and executive produces with Rossum (via her Composition 8 banner), Ronald Bass, Matt Olmstead, Sam Hoffman and Brian Kirk, who also directed the first two episodes. It is an unusually early pickup by the Disney streamer which (like other platforms) usually waits for long-tail viewership data before making renewal decision. Furious is still rolling out its first season, with the season finale, written by Meriwether, premiering Aug. 31. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Cancellations Photo Gallery: Series Ending This Year & Beyond The pickup of Furious follows t he cancellation earlier this week of another freshman Hulu origina l, comedy Not Suitable For Work , which was done two months after that series’ finale. Hulu has not released ratings data for Furious yet but noted in the renewal announcement that viewership has been growing week over week. Watch on Deadline Nielsen’s reporting is delayed, with numbers for Furious ‘ launch week coming out later today. Despite premiering with only three episodes vs. full-season drops for many streaming series, Furious is rumored to have cracked the Top 10 for streaming originals, which is based on total minutes consumed. Despite its staggered release, Furious also has been a consistent presence on Luminate’s weekly rankings, peaking at No.5 with 2.43M U.S. views for its first full week of release. Additionally, Furious is believed to be the #1 series on Disney+/Hulu worldwide for the month of August and the #2 freshman drama on Hulu in the U.S. year to date, with 4B cross-media impressions. Furious ‘ solid performance, coupled with its 98% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes and reasonable cost by streaming standards likely tipped the scale for an early renewal. Both walk their own paths toward justice, and as their lives start to intertwine, the line between right and wrong begins to blur. Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Scoot McNairy star alongside Rossum and Petticrew; Jake Lacy, Rob Delaney, Hope Davis, Rob Yang and Steve Way guest starred in Season 1, which was also executive produced by Rossum for Composition 8, along with Ronald Bass, Matt Olmstead, and Sam Hoffman. Brian Kirk executive produced and directed episodes 101 and 102. Furious is now streaming on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ in the US for bundle subscribers and on Disney+ internationally. title: Dolly Parton’s Sister Stella Says Late Icon Offered to Test Experimental Drugs to Help Battle Cancer
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All August 27, 2026 11:58am Stella and Dolly Parton Terry Wyatt/Getty Images Dolly Parton ’s little sister Stella Parton has revealed the country music icon asked her medical team to try experimental drugs on her to help future cancer patients battle their own health struggles. “What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future, Stella Parton said in an emotional Facebook tribute. She insisted the late icon got to heaven “right on time” on Tuesday, when Dolly Parton’s death after a brief battle with cancer was revealed. The music legend was admitted to the hospital in Nashville late last week after dealing with kidney and autoimmune issues. Related Stories Music Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton at Madison Square Garden Residency Opening Night: "We Love You" Music Dolly Parton's Spotify Streams Spiked Over 1,200 Percent Following Icon's Death Stella Parton said her sister’s 11th hour medical request that her doctors be allowed to test possibly future drugs to battle cancer was in keeping with her lifetime of trying to help others. “My sister was always thinking of others, and if you want to honor her legacy, show more kindness, lift others up and give more of your time and resources as she continued to do to the very end,” Stella Parton wrote. The elder Parton revealed in September that she was postponing a set of Las Vegas concerts to deal with “some health challenges.” In the past few months, the country music legend put on a brave front, telling her fans that she was OK. Her husband of nearly 58 years, businessman Carl Dean, died at age 82 on March 3, 2025. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to The Dolly Parton Estate for comment on Stella Parton’s social media tribute. Stella Parton’s tribute to her sister follows in full: My big sister Dolly got her wings this past Tuesday. If anyone gets to heaven I’m sure she made it right on time. I know she’s showing out big time, in all her sparkles and shine. That was my sister’s way. Every Tuesday about this time, before the sun came up and the world was still asleep, she and I for many years had our coffee together over the phone. Being little farm girls we’ve continued to be early risers. As she liked to say; “shoot Tedda we get more work done before the sun comes up than most folks do all day long!” We would catch up on gossip, as sisters do, and drink coffee and make plans as it has always been our way. My sister was one of the most generous, thoughtful and kind people I’ve ever known. What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future. My sister was always thinking of others and if you want to honor her legacy, show more kindness, lift others up and give more of your time and resources as she continued to do to the very end. I want to personally thank all of you for the out pouring of love and respect you are showing my sister. Your love and respect for her is deeply felt by all of us who loved her first and it helps as we grieve her passing through our lives! title: Tim Curry Remembered By ‘Rocky Horror Show’ Playwright Richard O’Brien & The Broadway Revival
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Anna Louizos Dies: Broadway Scenic Designer Of ‘In The Heights’ & ‘Avenue Q’ Was 69 Samuel Monroe Jr. Dies: ‘Menace II Society’ Actor Was 52 Rosie O’Donnell Joins Producing Team Of London-Bound Musical ‘Indigo’ About Autistic Teenager View All August 27, 2026 11:51am Tim Curry, 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' (1975) 20th Century Fox Film Corp./Everett Collection UPDATE, with tribute from playwright Richard O’Brien: Richard O’Brien, who wrote The Rocky Horror Show and cast his friend Tim Curry in the central role of Frank-N-Furter back in the ’70s, joined the current Broadway revival in offering up a heartfelt tribute to the late actor who died Tuesday at the age of 80. In a message written by O’Brien (who also played Riff Raff in both the stage musical and film) and posted on Instagram by his son Linus O’Brien, the playwright writes, “It is with an exceptionally sad heart and misted-up eyes that I share these words with you. Tim Curry was a wonderful man by nature who was also a wonderful performer and understood the difference between such delightful achievements. He never sought attention and never put himself before the roles that he played. He was, in short, a good egg and class act. It was both a privilege and delight to have known him and worked with him. Rest in peace dear Tim.” Related Stories News Tim Curry Dies: ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’ Actor Was 80 News Luke Evans, ‘Clue’ Stars, Carol Burnett, Josh Gad & More Pay Tribute To Tim Curry Broadway’s hit Tony-nominated revival of The Rocky Horror Show also remembered the man who made Frank-N-Furter a style icon in high heels, garter-supported fishnets and skin-tight bodice and who embodied one of the most beloved, campiest characters to ever grace a midnight movie. Watch on Deadline Richard O’Brien, Tim Curry and Patricia Quinn in ‘ The Rocky Horror Picture Show ‘ (1975) 20th Century Fox/Everett Collection In a post on the production’s Instagram page, the show writes, alongside a photo of Curry in character from The Rocky Horror Picture Show , “Remembering the legendary Tim Curry, who first brought Frank-N-Furter to life. We are heartbroken by his passing and grateful for the unforgettable legacy he leaves behind. Thank you, Tim, for giving the world a little more freedom, a little more fearlessness, and through the tears in our eyes, the courage to BE IT. We love you.” The “BE IT” line references one of Rocky Horror ‘s most famous catchphrases: “Don’t dream it, be it.” Although a flop when Curry led the cast in its original 1975 Broadway staging, panned by critics and closing after just 45 performances, the musical was revived for a more successful run in a 2002 Circle in the Square staging starring Tom Hewitt, Lea DeLaria, Jarrod Emick and Joan Jett. An even bigger hit revival arrived at Broadway’s Studio 54 venue last March in the Sam Pinkleton-directed staging starring Luke Evans (in the Frank-N-Furter role), Rachel Dratch, Andrew Durand, Amber Gray, Stephanie Hsu and Juliette Lewis. Last week, The Rocky Horror Show grossed a big $949,446 for the final week or original cast members Evans, Hsu and Durand. Jake Shears takes over for Evans on September 11, with Lorna Courtney and Kevin McHale joining the cast August 25. title: What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’
full_text: Aug 27, 2026 11:32am PT What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’ By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks 27 minutes ago What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’ 1 hour ago New York Comic Con Unveils 2026 Professional Schedule Lineup, Including ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ Author-NBCUniversal TV Panel (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago See All Audible More than half of Americans aged 18 and older, an estimated 157 million people, have listened to an audiobook, according to the Audio Publishers Association. Back in May, Audible likely added a few more to the fold with its Story House experience, which the Amazon-owned audiobook company proclaimed to be the first ever “bookless bookstore.” Following a pop-up during the return of BookCon at NYC’s Javits Convention Center in April, the Audible Story House operated for a month (from May 1-May 31) in lower Manhattan and saw more than 7,000 unique visitors come through its free-to-enter doors. Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 “What I was excited about was the opportunity to learn a lot more about customers and their experiences in that space,” Audible’s global head of brand content marketing James Finn tells Variety . “And oftentimes, I don’t have a sample size like that, and I don’t have a situation where we show up for an entire month in a city like New York and really learn more about our existing customers and new listeners.” Popular on Variety Nick Castle Located at 260 Bowery, the three-floor audiobook space offered guests the chance to browse titles using physical “Story Tiles” (blocks with RFID chips that made listening to samples via speakers, headphones or through your own phone and earbuds a quick business) throughout seven distinct listening spaces. It housed an immersive listening theater with Dolby Atmos surround sound and a “Listening Bar” with a dedicated “Story Tender” staffer offering up personalized recommendations for sampling. There were creator programming and panels, book clubs, hands-on crafting activities, a pop-up cafe from Brooklyn’s Land to Sea and tons of merch. But come June, it was all gone. “It was very hard when we closed the doors, I will be honest,” Finn says. “And a lot of people assumed that it was going to be there permanently, which was a nice compliment to the team that built the space.” Out of the 301 titles that were on offer in Audible’s Story House (“We never say what the one title is because everybody had an opinion — but we wanted to add that one more,” Finn says) 98% of the audiobooks were listened to “to any degree” over the course of the month in operation. The most popular included “Project Hail Mary,” “The Hive: A Thriller,” “George Orwell’s 1984,” “Just Kiss Already,” and Audible’s full-cast recording of “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone.” Photo by Bryan Bedder/Getty Images for Audible Getty Images for Audible There was also a lot of interest in Matt Dinniman’s “Dungeon Crawler Carl” LitRPG series, which released new book, “A Parade of Horribles” on May 12. “People were coming in, and they had already listened to it, and the eighth book had only come out a couple days ahead of time, and they were still tapping it, and they still were excited about that,” Finn says. But it wasn’t just the “Carl” fans that were sticking around. Audible says it counted more than 15,000 “deep engagement” experiences among its Story House guests, meaning the person did more than simply enter the space and browse. “People weren’t just coming in and then leaving, or coming in and listening to a sample and leaving,” Finn says. “They genuinely were staying around, going to the different areas, or coming to the community sessions where we had different activities, or going up to the cafe and buying an AudiBuddy and that was really interesting.” Finn says the Audible team has also been looking at “what are the learnings from the actual experience in New York that we can adapt to the experience within the app and within the service.” The biggest takeaway: “removing friction and allowing more engagement and allowing more of an opportunity for personalization, so that they have the opportunity to go to what’s interesting to them, but to sample and to try.” Audible Audible now has those 13,000 leftover “Story Tiles,” so there are some plans for what to do with those tactile representations of audiobooks. “We created that technology and that item. It didn’t exist,” Finn says. “The ambition was, how do we take something invisible and make it tangible? So the RFID component with it, we were able to see what people were listening to, and it was fantastic because everybody has different tastes and we saw such an interesting read across the entire slate of content there.” Finn adds: “But after the fact, what we’ve been doing is assessing what does Audible Story House look like in our plans for ’27. Right now, what we’re doing is similar to what you saw at BookCon. We’re going to bring a version of that with the core fundamentals to Guadalajara Book Festival, and then Frankfurt Book Fair.” Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Raye Make Mercury Prize Shortlist Loading comments... title: Oscars: 7 Films That Could Define the Awards Season, From ‘The Odyssey’ to ‘Michael’
full_text: Focus Features; A24; Lionsgate The frontrunners have a head start. The festivals have contenders ready to run them down. Let the games begin. The film year has already delivered, led by Christopher Nolan’s “ The Odyssey ,” a July event picture that doubled as the first true best picture launch of 2026. Back in May, Cannes fired the opening shots, sending Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” Netflix-acquired Spanish-language epic “La Bola Negra” and Russian drama “Minotaur” down the Croisette with buzz that will trail them into the fall. Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 But a frontrunner in August is just a film with an earlier release date. Over the next six weeks, the Oscars race will unspool in waves — the thin air of Telluride, the carpets of Venice’s Lido, the crowds of Toronto, the tastemakers of New York — with a single afternoon screening able to rewrite the whole narrative. Popular on Variety The festivals are set, and the year is loaded. And a moonwalk, a Homeric voyage and a Pixar goodbye are all in play at the same time. Here’s where the race stands. PROJECT HAIL MARY, Ryan Gosling, 2026. © Amazon MGM Studios /Courtesy Everett Collection ©MGM/Courtesy Everett Collection “Project Hail Mary” (Amazon MGM Studios) Ryan Gosling has three Oscar nominations — for “Half Nelson,” “La La Land” and “Barbie” — and no wins, and this adaptation of Andy Weir’s novel could hand him another shot. It also marks the live-action sci-fi leap of Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, the “Lego Movie” and “21 Jump Street” duo. Oscar history isn’t usually kind to directing partnerships: Only a handful have been nominated, most recently the Daniels for “Everything Everywhere All at Once.” Lord and Miller could join that short list, if Amazon MGM builds a friendly reminder campaign around them. “The Odyssey” (Universal Pictures) No surprise, Nolan is the man to beat, and “The Odyssey” is exactly the kind of feat the Academy’s directors branch loves to reward. His adaptation of Homer’s epic arrived to a wave of critical love, the rare summer tentpole with awards ambition built into its foundation: mythic source material, a starry ensemble and a theatrical approach designed to make the format itself part of the conversation. Two years after the “Oppenheimer” sweep — his first directing Oscar and a best picture win shared with wife and producing partner Emma Thomas — Nolan enters this campaign with a lot of Academy goodwill. Matt Damon’s Odysseus could put him in serious play in the actor race after winning a screenwriting Oscar nearly 30 years ago for “Good Will Hunting.” At the same time, John Leguizamo, Robert Pattinson, Anne Hathaway and Samantha Morton crowd a supporting field. Jaafar Jackson as Michael Jackson in Michael. Photo Credit: Courtesy of Lionsgate Courtesy of Lionsgate “Michael” (Lionsgate) Every season has an unofficial Oscar “villain” — think “Green Book,” “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Emilia Pérez.” This year has a moonwalk. “Michael” doesn’t need critics (it has a 38% Rotten score, but a 97% Certified Fresh rating); it needs the Academy’s populist wing, the same bloc that widened best picture to 10 slots after the 2008 “Dark Knight” snub to make room for films the public embraced. Jaafar Jackson’s transformation into the King of Pop will be the main talking point, and two-time Oscar nominee Colman Domingo’s chilling turn as family patriarch Joe Jackson lends the film gravity. Factor in the craft branches — editing, sound and makeup and hairstyling — and voters have plenty of boxes to check. Olivia Wilde, Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton appear in The Invite by Olivia Wilde, an official selection of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. Courtesy of Sundance Institute | photo c/o The Invite The Invite “The Invite” (A24) Olivia Wilde’s third feature is her sleekest, most assured work behind the camera, and A24 is mounting a full fall campaign. An English-language remake of Cesc Gay’s “The People Upstairs,” it boasts one of the year’s most impeccable ensembles: Seth Rogen, Wilde, four-time nominee Edward Norton and Oscar winner Penélope Cruz (a triple threat this year, with “La Bola Negra” and “Bunker” still to come). The engine is a crackling script by Rashida Jones and Will McCormack (reunited after “Celeste and Jesse Forever”) that offers sharp dialogue, a merciless structure and relentless laughs. In a season that rewards originals and adaptations alike, this is writing voters will likely remember in January and a cast the actors branch can get behind. OBSESSION, Inde Navarrette, 2025. © Focus Features /Courtesy Everett Collection ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection “Obsession” (Focus Features) If “Get Out” had Daniel Kaluuya, “Obsession” has Inde Navarrette. The horror breakout — the highest-grossing film in Focus Features history — lives and dies by its star, who plays a hypnotized co-worker and love interest with fearless physicality. Destined to be one of the year’s signature discoveries, as proven by her casting as Rogue in the upcoming “X-Men” movie, Navarrette could emerge as a critics’ awards darling, and Focus has every reason to push hard — perhaps even for writer-director-editor Curry Barker and a best picture slot. “I Swear” Graeme Hunter Pictures “I Swear” (Sony Pictures Classics) The N-word outburst at the BAFTA Awards put “I Swear” in the headlines and buried the real story: Robert Aramayo deserved that surprise win for lead actor. As a man living with Tourette’s syndrome, the 33-year-old English actor delivered an invigorating, deeply human turn that topped Timothée Chalamet’s in “Marty Supreme” and Michael B. Jordan’s in “Sinners.” The film’s U.S. release date makes it eligible for the Golden Globes, Critics Choice and the Oscars. If enough voters see it, they’ll understand why Aramayo won the BAFTA — and the film could get other Oscar nominations, including original screenplay. TOY STORY 5 , from left: Bullseye, Jessie (voice: Joan Cusack), 2026. © Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection ©Walt Disney Co./Courtesy Everett Collection “Toy Story 5” (Pixar) “Toy Story 5” is a $1 billion juggernaut and the kind of overwhelming favorite the category bends around; Pixar sequels lock up nominations before the competition has finished storyboarding. The film also gets a boost from legendary composer Randy Newman and superstar Taylor Swift. The franchise carries a perfect Oscar record: All four previous “Toy Story” films earned best original song nominations, the only series with a flawless mark in the category. Pixar could extend the streak with “I Knew It, I Knew You,” written by Swift and Jack Antonoff — which would also hand Swift, a record four-time album of the year Grammy winner, her first Oscar bid after two near misses. In a franchise built on goodbyes, one more song may be all it takes. title: New Edinburgh TV Event Confirmed At Launch Event Attended By Richard Gadd
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style “Public Service Algorithm” Propelled By Creators Prime Video Sets Access Doc Series On Peter Crouch & Abby Clancy Prime Video Revs Up Doc Series About F1 Driver Lando Norris View All August 27, 2026 11:15am Richard Gadd and Phoebe Waller-Bridge were discovered in Edinburgh Josh Telles for Deadline/Getty Edinburgh will have a TV festival in August after all. Scotland’s Cabinet Secretary for Education, Culture and Gaelic, Màiri McAllan, has today confirmed an initiative aimed at developing a new festival that will sit alongside the other Edinburgh festivals, including the film and comedy events. This confirms Deadline’s scoop from last month . This outlined how Screen Scotland had commissioned a piece of work aimed at exploring an industry event that would replace the Edinburgh TV Festival , which is next year moving to Manchester after 51 years. Related Stories News 'The Pitt' & 'The Celebrity Traitors' Win Prizes At Edinburgh TV Festival Awards News BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style "Public Service Algorithm" Propelled By Creators A launch event attended by Baby Reindeer and Half Man creator Richard Gadd was held today in Scotland’s capital, as many of the UK’s TV sector attended the final Edinburgh TV Festival, which is held at the Edinburgh International Conference Centre. Gadd and the likes of Fleabag creator Phoebe Waller-Bridge were discovered by the TV industry while performing their shows in the city during August. Watch on Deadline As we previously reported, the initial development work was funded by Screen Scotland and completed in early summer 2026. Per a news release today, this was undertaken “with fresh eyes” and explored “how Edinburgh’s August festivals partner to present a new offer to the global content industries, in response to the increasingly blurred boundaries between the different creative artforms and the way creative talent, IP and ideas move fluidly between them.” Former Edinburgh TV Festival Creative Director Rowan Woods , who oversaw the initial development, has been appointed to lead the next stage of development, which will again be funded by Screen Scotland and delivered through The Fringe Society. Working with the Fringe Society, Screen Scotland and a broader advisory group, she will consult widely across the August festivals and with venues, broadcasters, platforms, content creators, publishers and other potential participants and audiences to establish the shape of the new initiative. This will include “how it can best support the connection of new talent and IP to content commissioners worldwide.” This consultation phase is expected to conclude in early spring 2027, with an initial pilot planned for next August. This will likely place it in direct competition with the Manchester event, whose details haven’t yet been announced. Edinburgh is awash with energy during August, with the Fringe attracting hundreds of comedy acts, who perform in venues across the city during the month. Alongside that is the Edinburght Film Festival, the Edinburgh TV Festival and the Edinburgh International Book Festival, making the city a hive of activity. Many TV professional bemoaned the plan to move the TV fest out, even though costs have become prohibitively high in many cases. The Scottish Government is providing funding support for the new event’s development via Screen Scotland. More details will follow next year. David Smith, Director of Screen Scotland, said: “Edinburgh has a unique role to play in bringing together the people, ideas and creative work that will shape the future of the screen and wider creative industries. Every August, the city becomes a remarkable meeting place for talent from around the world, alongside audiences, producers, commissioners, artists and creative thinkers. “We have an opportunity to build on that extraordinary concentration of talent and energy and create something new, ambitious and genuinely distinctive for the global industry.” Separately, Screen Scotland is establish the Lynda Myles Debate as a keynote element of the August festivals from from next. This will “honour the contribution” of Lynda Myles, formerly Director of the Edinburgh International Film Festival and co-creator of the Edinburgh TV Festival, to the city’s festival month. “I’m deeply touched and honoured to have the debate named after me,” said Myles. title: Penn Badgley to Star in Murder Mystery ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ at Prime Video
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 11:00am Penn Badgley and David Hemingson Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images; Luke Fontana Logo text Penn Badgley just can’t seem to get away from killers. The You star will topline a murder mystery at Prime Video called Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone . Prime has placed a series order for the project from showrunner David Hemingson, Fifth Season and Made Up Stories. The series is based on a novel of the same name by Benjamin Stevenson. “I’m thrilled to be partnered with Fifth Season and Made Up Stories in bringing Ben’s heartfelt and darkly hilarious whodunit to life,” said Hemingson ( The Holdovers ). “And we are so lucky to have Penn as our lead. I can’t think of any actor better suited to bring Ern’s intensity, brilliance and hilariously dry sense of humor to life.” Related Stories TV Carina Walker Named Head of YA at Amazon MGM Studios Beyond the Book Anna Todd's Post-'After' Era: Inside Her Next Chapter With 'The Last Sunrise' Romance Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone follows Ern Cunningham (Badgley), a “mystery-writing expert” who heads to Vermont for family reunion “to welcome his brother Michael home from prison — the same brother Ern helped convict,” the show’s logline reads. “When a frozen body appears and a snowstorm traps everyone inside, the deaths begin to mount. Everyone in Ern’s family has already killed someone — either by accident or otherwise.” Hemingson will executive produce the series with Bruna Papandrea , Steve Hutensky and Jeanne Snow of Made Up Stories, Molly Allen, Badgley and Stevenson. “I am blown away by the vision and enthusiasm everyone has for bringing this book, and Ernest Cunningham, to the screen,” said Stevenson. “Penn perfectly captures Ern’s clueyness and cleverness, and David has brought bags of wit and heart to the script. With the passion of Amazon MGM Studios, Bruna and Steve behind us we have an absolutely killer team, and I can’t wait to solve a murder with them.” Stevenson’s 2022 novel kicked off a best-selling series — there are currently four Ernest Cunningham mysteries, and the author is writing a fifth. “We’re beyond excited to bring Ben’s sensational book to life in Dave Hemingson’s brilliant hands,” said Papandrea and Hutensky. “We’ve found the perfect Ern in Penn and it’s a dream to be making this series with our amazing partners Amazon MGM Studios and Fifth Season.” Added Peter Friedlander, head of global TV at Amazon MGM, “ Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone is a brilliantly inventive series that subverts the murder mystery genre in the most unexpected and entertaining ways. Ben created a world that is darkly funny and wickedly clever. Paired with David’s sharp storytelling and Penn’s magnetic presence, and with our incredible partners at Fifth season and Made Up Stories, this series is going to be something truly special for Prime Video.” Badgley is repped by Brillstein Entertainment Partners, CAA, The Lede Company and Hansen Jacobson. Hemingson is with by 3 Arts, WME, and McKuin Frankel. Stevenson is repped by Intellectual Property Group and Curtis Brown Australia. THR

title: Amazon MGM Orders Penn Badgley Murder Mystery Series ‘Everyone In My Family Has Killed Someone’ From David Hemingson
full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Andrew Bachelor Directs & Stars In Supernatural Horror Film ‘Tap Twice’ Amazon MGM Orders Penn Badgley Murder Mystery Series ‘Everyone In My Family Has Killed Someone’ From David Hemingson Jamie Dornan Joins Zoë Kravitz In Megan Park’s Mystery Apple Film View All August 27, 2026 11:00am Penn Badgley Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images Amazon MGM Studios has announced a series order for Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone , a darkly comedic murder mystery from Fifth Season and Made Up Stories, based on the bestselling book series by Benjamin Stevenson . You ‘s Penn Badgley will star, with David Hemingson ( The Holdovers ) set as showrunner and executive producer. Badgley returns to Amazon after wrapping a starring role opposite Meghann Fahy in their forthcoming rom-com You Deserve Each Other — also from Fifth Season, along with Likely Story. The project gets off the ground at Amazon MGM after an attempt at series development of the book at HBO. Related Stories Casting Elizabeth McGovern Joins Amazon MGM Horror Film 'Seasons' Executives Amazon MGM Studios Names Carina Walker Head Of YA Set deep in the dense mountains of Vermont’s Northeast Kingdom, Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone follows Ern Cunningham (Badgley), a mystery-writing expert who reluctantly attends a family reunion to welcome his brother Michael home from prison — the same brother Ern helped convict. When a frozen body appears and a snowstorm traps everyone inside, the deaths begin to mount. Everyone in his family has already killed someone — either by accident or otherwise. Watch on Deadline Mariner Books published the book in 2022. It’s Stevenson’s first in an internationally bestselling series, dubbed Ernest Cunningham Mysteries , whose fifth installment is currently in the works. Hemingson exec produces alongside Bruna Papandrea, Steve Hutensky and Jeanne Snow of Made Up Stories, Molly Allen, Badgley and Stevenson. Fifth Season and Made Up Stories are producing and will together serve as the studio. Fifth Season and Made Up Stories reteam following collaborations on series including The Good Daughter and Wolf Like Me for Peacock, Roar for Apple TV+, Nine Perfect Strangers for Hulu, Pieces of Her and Anatomy of a Scandal for Netflix, The Last Anniversary for AMC and The Lost Flowers of Alice Hart for Prime Video. In a statement on the series order, author Stevenson shared, “I am blown away by the vision and enthusiasm everyone has for bringing this book, and Ernest Cunningham, to the screen. Penn perfectly captures Ern’s clueyness and cleverness, and David has brought bags of wit and heart to the script. With the passion of Amazon MGM Studios, Bruna and Steve behind us we have an absolutely killer team, and I can’t wait to solve a murder with them!” Peter Friedlander, Amazon MGM’s Head of Global Television, added: “ Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone is a brilliantly inventive series that subverts the murder mystery genre in the most unexpected and entertaining ways. Ben created a world that is darkly funny and wickedly clever. Paired with David’s sharp storytelling and Penn’s magnetic presence, and with our incredible partners at Fifth Season and Made Up Stories, this series is going to be something truly special for Prime Video.” No stranger to murder, nor successful book adaptations, Badgley is coming off of a starring turn as serial killer Joe Goldberg in the hit thriller series You , based on the book series by Caroline Kepnes, which originated at Lifetime before moving to Netflix for its final four seasons. Otherwise best known for starring in The CW’s Gossip Girl , his upcoming slate includes the Bleecker Street thriller NDA , in addition to You Deserve Each Other . He is repped by Brillstein Entertainment Partners, CAA, and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller. Oscar-nominated for his script The Holdovers , the holiday dramedy directed for Focus Features by Alexander Payne, Hemingson also produced that film, marking the screen debut of Tony ‘s Dominic Sessa. Otherwise best known for creating the ABC series Whiskey Cavalier , the writer-producer has also worked on The Catch , Don’t Trust the B—- in Apartment 23 , Kitchen Confidential and myriad other series. He is repped by 3 Arts, WME, and McKuin Frankel & Whitehead. A stand-up comic, as well as an author, Stevenson’s books have sold over a million copies in 29 territories. The latest in his Ernest Cunningham series, Everyone in This Bank Is a Thief , released in March. He is repped by Leslie Conliffe at Intellectual Property Group and Pippa Masson at Curtis Brown Australia. title: How Dolly Parton Crossed Over Into Hollywood — and America’s Hearts
full_text: × Skip to main content By David Kamp Plus Icon David Kamp David Kamp | The Hollywood Reporter View All August 27, 2026 10:42am Nine to Five (1980): from left, Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton, Jane Fonda. 20th Century Fox Film Corp./Courtesy Everett Collection Dolly Parton was perfect for her breakout decade, the 1970s. Color TVs outsold black-and-white sets for the first time in 1972, the annus mirabilis in which she composed “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You,” allegedly on the same day. With her huge yellow hair, chambray-blue wardrobe, and sunshiny radiance, Parton was engineered to beam straight through the screen into every American home. Both of those songs became number-one country hits, in ’73 and ’74, respectively, and Dolly, Porter Wagoner’s girl singer no more, became America’s rhinestone superstar. The 70s were also the last golden age of an American monoculture, when most of us experienced the same programs, movies, and records at the same time. Country crossover wasn’t so much crossover as happy coexistence. Roy Clark could show up at Felix and Oscar’s New York apartment in The Odd Couple to demonstrate his virtuoso pickin’ skills and be summoned to Burbank to sub in for Johnny Carson as a guest host of The Tonight Show . Cliff Arquette’s hayseed character Charlie Weaver reliably occupied the lower left corner on Hollywood Squares . Hee Haw , the variety show Clark co-hosted with Buck Owens, thrived on TV in first-run syndication — it’s where this writer, like millions of other impressionable kids, first saw Parton perform “Coat of Many Colors,” her affecting song about the coat her mother sewed for her “from a box of rags that someone gave us.” Young Dolly wore the coat proudly to school, only to be ridiculed by mean kids who laughed at the sight of it. Dolly, unbowed, told off the poverty-shamers by saying she was actually rich, because of “the love my mama sewed in every stitch.” You couldn’t not be moved or besotted. Related Stories Music Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton at Madison Square Garden Residency Opening Night: "We Love You" Music Dolly Parton's Spotify Streams Spiked Over 1,200 Percent Following Icon's Death Of all the artists flying the country flag in this era, Dolly was the most transcendent, rivaled only by the great Johnny Cash. (Whereas Cash was known for his gravity and underrated comedically, Parton was known for her levity and underrated artistically.) Dolly was simply irresistible to everyone, no matter their background or cultural prejudices. Even the rock snobs at Rolling Stone loved her, flying her to New York in ’77 for an extraordinary photo shoot in which Annie Leibovitz paired Parton with an emerging Austrian bodybuilding star. While a naked Arnold Schwarzenegger stood with legs wide apart and biceps flexed, Parton, a pink bow in her hair, joyfully posed in front of him, her hips obscuring his naughty bits, her ginormously bewigged head blocking out his, eclipse-style. Parton, conversely, seemed to embrace all comers without wariness. In her successful bid to achieve crossover pop stardom, she sublimated her writer’s ego and turned to two old Brill Building hands, Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil, for “Here You Come Again,” which shot to number three on the Billboard Hot 100. When the Bee Gees were lying low in the post-disco backlash of the early 1980s, she and Kenny Rogers took their song “Islands in the Stream” to number one. On Dolly , her short-lived 1976 variety show, she gamely performed with collaborators both likely (e.g. Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris, later to rejoin Parton for their triumphant 1987 album Trio ) and perhaps not so much (e.g. The Hues Corporation, of “Rock the Boat” fame, and KC and the Sunshine Band). In 1978, a writer named Colin Irwin, of the British publication Melody Maker , described the process of having his snide-journo defenses dissolved by Parton in real time: For ten minutes I just gawp, unable to comprehend the vision, but she — o bviously well-acquainted with such a reaction — accepts it gracefully, perhaps even with relish, and rattles on… “Been a hectic day but ah’m pretty used t’that nahw an’ ah enjoy meetin’ new people cos ah get a lota ideas for songs because of certain personalities that ah meet. Mahbe ah’ll wraht a song ’bout yew. Ah’ll call it ‘Laughing Eyes.’” Sigh. I think I’m in love. Unquestionably, she manipulates the press . And yet you still love her. Because she admits it. Where others of the ilk make you cringe with their synthetic sincerity, Dolly is disarmingly honest about it all, constantly sending herself up, mockingly talking about her wigs and her figure. She admits that her bizarre stage act and her appearance are merely means to an end, and you can even forgive the weepy sentiment of so much of her material, born out of the stifling poverty in which she was brought up. “Coat Of Many Colors,” for example — which she has often cited as her favorite song — reconstructed the Joseph story in the Bible, but was also based on a traumatic experience she herself had as a child. How can anyone with a heart knock that? The great monoculture of which Parton was the apogee began to fall apart with the advent of cable television in the 1980s and was eventually atomized completely by the internet. Today we live in a world where someone named Ella Langley can occupy the upper reaches of the Billboard charts alongside someone named Lil Baby, the fans of one having no idea of what the other’s music even sounds like. But Dolly kept on Dollying, decade after decade, holding us all together when very little else did. At the dawn of the 80s, she effortlessly translated her talents to film, starring alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin in 9 to 5 and writing and performing its infectious title song. In 1986, she formed a production company, Sandollar Productions, with her former manager, Sandy Gallin, a gay, Jewish, very tan show-business macher . “Nobody could quite get how the Christian Southern girl and New York Jewish boy could have so much in common,” she told the New York Times when Gallin died, in 2017. “But it was real. My husband didn’t love to travel, and Sandy was gay and did.” Together, Parton and Gallin produced the Father of the Bride movies and the millennially revered Buffy the Vampire Slayer TV series. Dolly Parton and producer Sandy Gallin at the Beverly Hills Hotel in 1992. Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection/Getty Images With Gallin’s help, she also launched the theme park Dollywood, situated just outside her native Great Smoky Mountains, in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee. There, she turned her heritage, warts and all, into a celebration, complete with a museum of Partonian artifacts literally called Rags to Riches: The Dolly Parton Story. (It has since evolved into a formidable multimedia complex called The Dolly Parton Experience.) Unlike certain other claimants of Appalachian background, Parton related her stories of hillbilly hardship without grievance. Over and over, she chose positivity. She often related the story of how taken she was, as a small child, with the scarlet woman of her little town, “with this yellow hair piled on her head, bright red lipstick, red nails, and high-heeled shoes. I thought she was the prettiest thing I’d ever seen. I used to say to my mama, ‘Oh, she’s so pretty!’” When Dolly’s mother derided the woman as “trash,” Parton recalled, “I just thought, ‘That’s what I want to be when I grow up: trash!’” Opry-style humor aside, Parton took her platform as an odds-beater seriously. Convinced that her sharecropper father’s illiteracy prevented him from realizing his dreams, she founded a nonprofit called The Imagination Library that mails free books to children every month from birth to the age of five. Founded in 1995, the program has distributed more than 300 million books. Lee Parton was still alive when The Imagination Library was founded. “I had the idea to do something special for him,” Parton said in 2018. “In the bible, where it talks about ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ I don’t think that necessarily means just to obey them. It means to bring honor to their name if you can. So I got my daddy involved in this program. I wanted him to feel like he was part of something special. He took such pride in the fact that the little kids called me ‘The Book Lady.’ He was prouder of that than anything.” How can anyone with a heart knock that? Parton was studiedly apolitical yet anything but gutless. In 2020, in the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, she donated $1 million to Vanderbilt University Medical Center to seed the research that led to the development of the Moderna vaccine. In her words and deeds, she supported gay rights and marriage equality, arguing for the latter with the characteristic zinger, “Why can’t they be as miserable as us heterosexuals in their marriages?” Coming from someone else — really, anyone else — these pro-queer, pro-vax, and pro-literacy stances would likely have been critiqued in some quarters as “woke.” But you never hear anyone carping on TV or social media about “Dollyweird.” Parton was a uniter. She commanded a wonderfully anachronistic monocultural respect, attributable to all the goodwill she had accumulated and the positivity she never stopped projecting. We’ll truly never see Dolly’s like again, though you can see certain individuals modeling themselves in her likeness. Sabrina Carpenter paid explicit homage to Parton’s comic-blond-minx persona by inviting the woman herself to record a duet, 2024’s “Please Please Please,” complete with a caper video that finds the pair sweetly harmonizing while a man they’ve abducted lies bound in the back of their pickup truck. Sabrina is no Dolly, which isn’t a knock but a comment on the impossibility of any new artist ever enjoying the level of admiration and adoration that Parton did for most of her life. But it’s great that Dolly remains, fifty-plus years after “Jolene” and the glory days of Hee Haw , an aspirational model. Her motto was, “Dream more, learn more, care more, and be more.” She more than lived up to it. THR

title: Will Forte Says Glowing Reviews for ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ “Make It Feel Like You’re Not Crazy,” Admits “I Felt Gaslit For a While”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 10:42am Will Forte at the 'Coyote vs. Acme' premiere at Westwood Village Theater on Wednesday night. Eric Charbonneau/Ketchup Entertainment via Getty Images After several years in limbo, Coyote vs. Acme finally got its moment in the sun on Wednesday at its L.A. premiere. It was a night that for a long time did not seem possible, after Warner Bros. Discovery shelved the film in November 2023 in favor of a tax write-off. Fans rallied around the project, though, refusing to let it die — until in March 2025, Ketchup Entertainment saved the film and set it up for a summer 2026 theatrical release. Star Will Forte looks back at that period as “an emotional roller coaster,” admitting that despite how vocal people were being online to revive the film, “I didn’t think it would do anything.” Related Stories TV Tom Colicchio Says 'Top Chef' Has Become as Important as a James Beard Award Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Hits No. 2 on All-Time Domestic Chart, Topping 'Avengers: Endgame' “I was just like, ‘They’re not hearing you, it’s not going to make a difference.’ And then they just kept going and it’s because of them the movie’s out,” Forte told The Hollywood Reporter on the carpet. “I had given up on it and I can’t thank these people enough. I always thought this movie was super special and the support from the community has meant so much. It’s made me feel sane; I felt gaslit for a while and their support, now the positive reviews coming out — [they] just make it feel like you’re not crazy.” Coyote vs. Acme is a hybrid live-action and animation movie set in the Looney Tunes universe. It sees Wile E. Coyote deciding to sue the Acme Corporation after their products fail him one too many times in his relentless pursuit of the Roadrunner, with Forte as his inexperienced lawyer and John Cena as Acme’s attorney. And as Forte mentioned, the film is being released amid glowing reviews and very positive audience buzz. “It’s so validating. I’ve been a part of a lot of projects that haven’t gotten great reviews that I have loved — MacGruber . I love it. People may hate it, but I love it, I’m so proud of it,” the actor said, noting that reviews are not everything but “in this case, I am accepting positive reviews and saying they do mean something, I’m doing a flip around.” He continued that much like Wile E. Coyote going up against a big corporation, the film itself is an underdog, “so we need all the help we can get, and it feels like all these voices, the voices that helped us get the movie into the theaters, are helping spread the word about it being in the theaters. Hopefully people will listen to them and see these positive views and go like, ‘This movie deserves to be seen.'” Cena echoed, “We’re here, we’re coming out in theaters, I just hope that everyone who used their voice shows up to see this thing.” Wile E. Coyote makes a grand entrance at the #CoyoteVsAcme premiere pic.twitter.com/4CjPnYTOcH — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) August 27, 2026 That appreciation for the fans was clear at the event as well, as a costumed Wile E. Coyote character marched down the carpet with the UCLA marching band, carrying a sign that read “Absolute Cinema.” It’s a reference to a viral video of a fan who picketed outside of the Warner Bros. lot, in the rain, following the film’s cancellation; the character also appeared inside the screening, with another sign that read, “Thank you fans.” “We feel so lucky,” emphasized director Dave Green . “Every single person that spoke out and tweeted and wrote a message, and for our brave costumed Coyote who stood out in the rain, we’re grateful for every single individual who was there for us.” The filmmaker also brushed off any initial sequel plans as “I’ve not thought beyond this day,” but noted, “We made a movie that we thought was funny and worked for us and we internally thought was a blast. It’s so validating and kind to see the audience responding.” Coyote vs. Acme, which also stars Lana Condor , Eric Bauza and Martha Kelly, hits theaters on Friday. THR

title: BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style “Public Service Algorithm” Propelled By Creators
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style “Public Service Algorithm” Propelled By Creators Prime Video Sets Access Doc Series On Peter Crouch & Abby Clancy Prime Video Revs Up Doc Series About F1 Driver Lando Norris View All August 27, 2026 10:37am BBC boss Matt Brittin BBC The BBC ‘s Director General, Matt Brittin , has said the British broadcaster’s streaming service could benefit from a “public service algorithm” that allows it to function more like YouTube. The striking plans, which Brittin warned was not “policy” at this stage, would see the BBC iPlayer opened up to creators and make the service more like YouTube, the platform that the exec oversaw in EMEA before joining the BBC. Related Stories News BBC Files New Motion To Dismiss Donald Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit, Challenges Claims Of U.S. Viewership Via VPN News Donald Trump Waging $10B Legal War Against BBC On Basis “Doctored” Documentary May Have Been Viewed 285 Times In America In his first address to the industry today at the Edinburgh TV Festival, the former Google exec once again warned the BBC iPlayer had “fallen behind” rivals due to a focus on content spend over technology in recent years. He first made similar noise in a town hall speech to staff in May soon after he became DG. Brittin was careful to say this was “no fault of the team” at the BBC and that the content spend meant he “inherited incredible audience reach,” but leaves a puzzle over the iPlayer’s future and an immediate challenge in improving the iPlayer recommendations functionality. Watch on Deadline His blue-sky solution was for the iPlayer to function more like YouTube by hosting creators from around the UK – “providing they stick to the guidelines we choose to set.” He didn’t detail how this would be achieved, what the remuneration offer would be or why creators would choose to opt for BBC digital services over YouTube or other social media platforms, but it is still one of the more tantalizing ideas to be floated by a director general of the BBC for some time. Brittin also called for the BBC to be “a more open platform” and that there was a need to “create sovereign media public space,” while adding the UK could build something “unadulterated by commercial interests, by algorithms that have other interests at heart.” The service, which he dubbed ‘iPlayer 2.0″, would be based around “educating, informing and entertaining the public here and ideally around the world,” he said, adding it should be created “it in a way that’s not biased towards the incentives of a U.S. tech company or commercial interests. It should be biased towards what we want public service to be all about.” It is likely the BBC, which is in the midst of cutting 2,000 roles to save around £500M ($679M), will have to cut programs to pay for improvements to the iPlayer. He noted that the BBC had shed £1.3B over the past decade and services and programs would inevitably come under pressure. Brittin has spent his first 100 days at the BBC travelling to different parts of the mammoth organization to identify where to prioritize his efforts and how to wrestle with the type of existential crisis that outgoing BBC presenter Amol Rajan described earlier today. Brittin admitted he had not “understood quite the severity” of the financial pressure heaped on the BBC. “Obviously, to get to that scale of savings, there’s uncertainty hanging over a lot more colleagues than those who will eventually leave the organization,” he added. “That’s really hard to deal with. title: Tyler Perry’s ‘Divorced Sistas’ & ‘Zatima’ Among 4 Former BET+ Series Renewed By Paramount+
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Tyler Perry’s ‘Divorced Sistas’ & ‘Zatima’ Among 4 Former BET+ Series Renewed By Paramount+ Rafe Judkins Inks Overall Deal With Paramount Television Studios As Paramount+ Ramps Up Worldbuilding Efforts Amazon MGM Studios Names Carina Walker Head Of YA View All August 27, 2026 10:30am Paramount+ EXCLUSIVE : Two months after BET+ was folded into Paramount+ , with its programming migrating to the larger streamer, four of the former BET+ original series have been renewed by Paramount+. They include Tyler Perry’s Divorced Sistas , picked up for Season 3, and Zatima (Season 6), as well as Carl Weber’s The Black Hamptons (Season 3) and The Family Business (Season 7). Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery News 2026 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable Divorced Sistas and Zatima ‘s orders are for 16 episodes, which is typical for Perry shows, running in two eight-episode installments. That has been the pattern for Divorced Sistas while Zatima ‘s seasons to date have consisted of 20 episodes, split in two batches of 10. That includes upcoming seasons of both series that had not been announced but had been quietly filming: a 20-episode fifth season of Zatima , and 16-episode second season of Divorced Sistas . The latter, a spinoff from Perry’s popular BET series Sistas , last summer logged the most watched series premiere on BET+. Watch on Deadline The Family Business and The Black Hamptons ’ pickups are for 10 episodes each. They are somewhat surprising given the large gap between seasons, especially for The Black Hamptons, whose renewal comes more than two and a half years after the series’ eight-episode second season ended its run on BET+. The Family Business ‘ 10-episode sixth season released its finale on Dec. 18 last year. It is possible that the renewals had been done unofficially awhile ago and are now being announced. The pickups for Divorced Sistas, Zatima, The Family Business and The Black Hamptons join the March Season 6 renewal for BET+ original comedy Ms. Pat Show, which was done ahead of BET+’s slate transition to Paramount+ in June. ‘We feel the migration was very successful, the audiences are showing up for sure, Paramount+ Head of Originals Jane Wiseman told Deadline last week, noting that the volume of originals that BET+ was known for is not going to go down now that the shows are on Paramount+. The integration of BET+ into Paramount+ involved Paramount buying out Tyler Perry Studios’ stake in BET+. He remains one of Paramount’s most prolific creators/producers across BET and Paramount+. “Our relationship with Tyler Perry is very strong, and I’m excited for more content from him, as well as working closely with our friends at BET Studios,” Wiseman said last week. BET Studios also works across Divorced Sistas, Zatima, The Family Business and The Black Hamptons . Here are details on the newly renewed series: Title: The Black Hamptons Season: 3 EPs: Carl Weber, ND Brown Jones, Trey Haley Logline: In this adaptation of Carl Weber’s novel, the Britton family faces high tensions with the newly arrived Johnsons in the upscale Black town of Sag Harbor, NY. Talent: Lamman Rucker, Vanessa Bell Calloway, Elise Neal, Brian White, Karon Riley, and Mike Merrill Episode count: 10 Eps Title: The Family Business Season: 7 EPs: Carl Weber, ND Brown Jones, Trey Haley, Ernie Hudson Logline: The wealthy Duncans run their lucrative New York-based criminal enterprise with iron fists, and family always comes first. Talent: Ernie Hudson, Valarie Pettiford, Darrin Dewitt, Javicia Leslie, Tami Roman, Sean Ringgold, Michael Jai White, Arrington Foster and Lisa Raye McCoy. Episode count: 10 Eps Title: Tyler Perry’s Divorced Sistas Season: 3 EPs: Created, directed, written and executive produced by Tyler Perry. Logline: What begins as one confession cracks open everything this group of women thought they were protecting. Years of deception, half-truths, and emotional compromises finally surface, forcing Rasheda, Geneva, Naomi, Tiffany, and Bridgette to confront not just the men in their lives, but one another. Talent: LeToya Luckett, Khadeen Indréa, Porscha Coleman, Briana Price, Jennifer Sears, DeVon Franklin, Ronreaco Lee, and Robert Christopher Riley. title: Miley Cyrus Remembers Godmother Dolly Parton: “I Have An Angel By My Side”
full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine Writers Guild Foundation Taps 2026 Veterans Fellowship Cohort Miley Cyrus Remembers Godmother Dolly Parton: “I Have An Angel By My Side” ‘The Secret Lives Of Mormon Wives’: Taylor Frankie Paul Faces ‘Bachelorette’ Backlash & Jen Affleck Confronts Whitney Leavitt In Season 5 Trailer View All August 26, 2026 9:52am Story Arc HANNAH MONTANA, Miley Cyrus, Dolly Parton, 'Good Golly, Miss Dolly', (Season 1, aired Sept. 29, 2006), 2006-, © Disney Channel / Courtesy Everett Collection Miley Cyrus mourned the loss of her godmother and mentor Dolly Parton , who died Tuesday at the age of 80 , writing in an Instagram post the following morning that “the feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share.” “Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” she wrote. “What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. 🦋” Cyrus concluded her emotional post: “I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things. 💖” Watch on Deadline View this post on Instagram Related Stories Culture Remembering Dolly Parton: A Career in Photos News Dolly Parton: Keke Palmer, Pedro Pascal, Kacey Musgraves & More Pay Tribute To “One Of One” Country Music Legend Cyrus has extremely close familial and creative ties to Parton, who had been part of the younger star’s life since she was born. “I’ve known her since she was a baby,” Parton told Good Morning America in 2009. “Her father’s a friend of mine, and when she was born, he said, ‘You just have to be her godmother,’ and I said, ‘I accept.’ We never did do a big ceremony, but I’m so proud of her, love her, and she’s just like one of my own.” In a post of his own on Tuesday, after news of Parton’s death broke, the Cyrus patriarch honored Parton: “Like every little boy, I grew up loving Dolly Parton. She was a part of our lives, on our TV’s, right in our living rooms,” he wrote, adding: “Dolly recently sent me a beautiful message, telling me she loved me with her whole heart. I will always love her in the same way ….. with my whole heart … and I always will.” Parton also played Cyrus’ on-screen godmother, occasionally appearing on Hannah Montana across its four seasons. They have taken to stage and screen together at various points over the years since. In 2022, the pair co-hosted NBC’s Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party from Miami, Florida, featuring joint performances of some of their hits including “Wrecking Ball” and “I Will Always Love You.” Cyrus and Parton also collaborated musically several times. Cyrus joined Parton in 2010 at the 25th anniversary of Dollywood to sing “Jolene” — a song she has performed many times over since then. They performed it again together in 2019 at the Grammy Awards. Cyrus also co-wrote a track on her 2017 album Younger Now with Parton, titled “Rainbowland,” and the elder singer recruited her goddaughter to appear on her A Holly Dolly Christmas album in 2020. CBS News and ABC News aired primetime specials that evening, and an NBC News special aired on Wednesday. PREVIOUSLY: CBS News and ABC News will air specials on Tuesday paying tribute to Dolly Parton, who died today at the age of 80. Watch on Deadline NBC plans a news special on Wednesday. A CBS News Special: Dolly Parton — An American Icon will air at 10 p.m. ET, with Gayle King and Tony Dokoupil along with a team of CBS News journalists commemorating Parton’s life. They will be joined by Anthony Mason, CBS News’ senior culture and senior national correspondent, and a correspondent in Dollywood in Tennessee.
